items.title: Ruth Brisbane interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 2, 2013
items.q: I had two younger sisters that I used to take to the Motown shows — Stevie Wonder and so forth

ctx.x: Well that was also an era of great soul music and Motown. Did that music catch your ear? Did you enjoy that kind of music? James Brown?

I heard of James Brown once — I mean not once but — I kept hearing about James Brown. I don’t know why I hadn’t heard him. But he was at the Apollo Theater on 125th Street so I made sure that I went to see him. And I thought he was hilarious, especially © Fillius Jazz Archive -5-

with the coat and everything, and the band. They all had a part doing something. And it was a repetitive show, but he had a long line around. I said what do I know? Boys, look at this. But the Motown sound came to me kind of late. And I say that because I had two younger sisters that I used to take to the Motown shows — Stevie Wonder and so forth — at the big theaters in Brooklyn and in Manhattan. And I could not get into it at the time.
